text:
Alex: Seeing a sudden throughput drop on eu-west-2 about 14:20 UTC, lots of worker restarts and GPU OOMs. Throughput down ~45% vs baseline.
Maya: Oof. Any correlation with recent rollouts?
Alex: deploy-bot reported a model variant rollout at 13:58 but it was a small routing change. Not obvious.
deploy-bot: @channel Completed rollout: routing delta -> variant-v2 (canary 10%).
Sanjay: I pulled the perf dashboard: latency p95 spiked, and KV cache hitrate fell from 92% -> 61% around the same time. Looks like cache region churn.
Liam: Also seeing free-list churn in allocator metrics, fragmentation up on all GPUs. Could cause OOMs as effective contiguous memory drops.
Alex: attaching profiler snapshot (trimmed).
Alex: ```
GPU0: free_contig_max: 1.2GB  total_free: 6.4GB  fragmentation_index: 0.81
GPU1: free_contig_max: 600MB  total_free: 6.0GB  fragmentation_index: 0.9
worker_restarts: 7 within 10m
kv_cache_evictions/sec: 350 -> 1200
batch_size_median: 2 -> 1
```
Maya: Batch sizes collapsing to 1 explains throughput drop; batching heuristics likely got starved by latency spikes. If KV evictions increase, more token recompute and larger memory churn.
Sanjay: Kernel selection traces show several fallback kernels chosen after a few seconds under memory pressure, e.g., switched to slower quantized kernels causing per-token latency to increase.
Liam: Can we confirm noisy tenant? Any tenant with sudden spike in long sequences or big prefix?
Alex: Tenant A had a burst of long-ctx requests around 14:15 (logs: seq_len avg 2048 -> 8192 for 200 reqs). That aligns with the first restart.
Maya: So chain: long sequences from Tenant A -> KV cache bloat and prefix population -> allocator fragmentation -> not enough contiguous for large KV pages -> OOMs and worker restarts -> fallback kernels and batching collapse -> throughput drop.
Sanjay: I ran a quick simulation locally reproducing eviction ripple when many long sequences populate large KV segments; eviction policy is LRU and we haven't isolated per-tenant quotas here.
Alex: Temporary mitigation: throttle Tenant A and scale up dedicated pool for eu-west-2. Can ops apply a soft throttling rule? @Liam can you coordinate?
Liam: On it. Pushing rate-limit rule and adding a transient dedicated node.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-1842725000 - \"eu-west throughput drop: OOM + cache churn\" assigned to eng-runtime.
Maya: Longer term: two action items — 1) add per-tenant KV caps and priority-aware eviction, 2) make batching heuristic resilient to transient p95 spikes (don't immediately collapse to size 1).
Sanjay: Also add a kernel-selection guard: if fragmentation high, prefer kernels that reduce allocations even if slightly slower, to avoid OOM restart cycles.
Alex: I'll open a follow-up RFC for prioritized KV quotas + batching hysteresis. Maya, Sanjay — can you own prototypes?
Maya: Yep, I'll prototype batching hysteresis knob (hold previous batch size for N seconds if throughput > threshold).
Sanjay: I'll prototype per-tenant kv caps + eviction priority.
Liam: Update: throttling rule applied to Tenant A, added a spare node to the pool. Early signs: kv_evictions/sec down to 420, worker restarts stopped.
Alex: Great. Keep monitoring for the next 30m and collect a full flamegraph sample if it stabilizes.
Maya: Adding alert: fragmentation_index > 0.75 && kv_evictions/sec > 300 -> page us in incidents.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Postmortem draft once we stabilize. :thumbsup:\"
